raw_case_text: A 75-year-old male from Algeria had HIV infection since 2001 treated with nevirapine and lamivudine/zidovudine. He had cerebral toxoplasmosis, chronic hepatitis B, gastrointestinal CMV infection, and anal squamous cell carcinoma. In 2013, the patient started treatment with darunavir, ritonavir, raltegravir and emtricitabine. VL had been diagnosed in 2001, and treated with L-AmB 5 mg/Kg/d for 15 days with partial improvement. Maintenance therapy of 3 mg/kg weekly was planned but irregularly administered. Recurrence was reported in March 2011, the infecting specie was identified as L. infantum. The number of CD4 lymphocytes was 33/mm3, and viral load 75000 copies/mL. The patient received 40 mg/kg of L-AmB, followed by 3 mg/kg at 15-day interval. Clinical improvement was obtained but qualitative PCR remained positive. In 2012, L-AmB infusions were administered at 3-week intervals. In 2013, a last course of 50 mg/kg of L-AmB was administered, Despite this complete course of L-AmB, clinical symptoms worsened (weight loss, fatigue), clinical splenomegaly was present (greater diameter 20 cm on the CT scan), and parasitemia remained positive and stable (from 126 Leishmania/ml before treatment to 118 Leishmania/ml after completion of the course 3 weeks later). Meglumine antimoniate was thus administered, initially at low doses (4-10 mg/kg SbV every other day for 7 weeks) because of advanced age. Treatment was well tolerated except for moderate neutropenia. Fatigue resolved and weight increased from 50 to 61 Kg. The spleen was no longer palpable after 2 months of treatment. Number of CD4 lymphocytes increased from 75 to 134/mm3. Parasitemia cleared and remained negative through 13 months of follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 75-year-old male with HIV infection presented with worsening fatigue, weight loss, and marked splenomegaly.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 75-year-old male with HIV infection diagnosed in 2001 and visceral leishmaniasis diagnosed in 2001 presented with recurrent disease. He experienced a relapse in March 2011 treated with L-AmB (40 mg/kg, then biweekly maintenance), but qualitative PCR remained positive. In 2012, L-AmB was given every 3 weeks. In 2013, despite a full 50 mg/kg course of L-AmB, he deteriorated with progressive weight loss (weight 50 kg), profound fatigue, persistent massive splenomegaly, and unchanged parasitemia. He was treated with low-dose meglumine antimoniate, which produced rapid recovery.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection diagnosed in 2001 (initially treated with nevirapine and lamivudine/zidovudine; switched in 2013 to darunavir, ritonavir, raltegravir, and emtricitabine). Past medical history included cerebral toxoplasmosis, chronic hepatitis B, gastrointestinal cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection, and anal squamous cell carcinoma. Visceral leishmaniasis diagnosed in 2001.
subjective.review_of_systems: Severe fatigue, unintentional weight loss, abdominal heaviness and fullness. Denied fever, vomiting, or diarrhea.

objective.physical_examination: Elderly, wasted male; body weight 50 kg (increased to 61 kg post-treatment). Abdominal examination revealed marked palpable splenomegaly (spleen became non-palpable after 2 months of antimonial therapy).
objective.routine_investigations: In March 2011: CD4+ count 33/mm^3, HIV viral load 75,000 copies/mL. During antimonial therapy: moderate neutropenia without other toxicities. Post-treatment: CD4+ count increased from 75 to 134/mm^3.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan demonstrated massive splenomegaly with a maximum diameter of 20 cm.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive Diagnosis: Liposomal amphotericin B-refractory recurrent visceral leishmaniasis in an elderly patient with advanced HIV-1 coinfection and multiple opportunistic infections.
Diagnostic Confirmation: Parasite identified as Leishmania infantum in March 2011. Quantitative peripheral blood PCR demonstrated persistent parasitemia (126 Leishmania/mL prior to 2013 L-AmB course, remaining at 118 Leishmania/mL after completion).
Differentials Ruled Out: Progression of opportunistic infections (toxoplasmosis, CMV, hepatitis B), hematologic malignancy, and anal carcinoma metastasis.
Treatment & Clinical Course: Demonstrated clinical and parasitological failure to high-dose liposomal amphotericin B regimens (including 40 mg/kg and 50 mg/kg cumulative courses). Successfully treated with low-dose meglumine antimoniate (4-10 mg/kg SbV every other day for 7 weeks) adjusted for advanced age. Treatment was well tolerated aside from moderate neutropenia, resulting in complete resolution of fatigue, weight gain of 11 kg, disappearance of splenomegaly, CD4+ increase to 134/mm^3, and sustained clearance of blood parasitemia through 13 months of follow-up.
